text: 20.02 EDT Cabinet never discussed cutting refugee intake, says Plibersek Tanya Plibersek has said cabinet never discussed cutting Australia’s refugee intake after debate and confusion within Labor came into public view this week. The Financial Review on Thursday reported the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, was planning to cut intake of 20,000 arrivals to 13,750 in 2027-28. The prime minister declared the figure would stay at 20,000 after Labor MPs and refugee advocates reacted angrily. Asked on the ABC’s Insiders if the government had considered a cut to the refugee intake, Plibersek said: No, I don’t really know where this story came from. We reconfirmed our number as recently as a month ago at the national conference. There was certainly no discussion in cabinet. She said the 20,000-a-year figure was a “permanent commitment”. The party’s most recent national conference voted to approve a statement that read: Labor will seek, in the short term, to maintain Australia’s government funded humanitarian intake numbers at 20,000 places per year while also continuing to aspire to achieving 27,000 places per year.
author: Luca Ittimani
